summary: Suspected OAuth app–linked service-account provisioning after external Google Drive share
description: Summary: Security team detected an anomalous spike in service-account creation and OAuth token exchange shortly after a third-party Google Drive share was accepted by an internal user. Access patterns indicate a newly authorized OAuth app performed API calls to the internal provisioning API (svc-provision) resulting in two short-lived service accounts and multiple role bindings to infra:deploy roles. This ticket tracks triage, containment, and remediation.
impact: Potential unauthorized provisioning of service accounts with infra:deploy role in prod regions. No confirmed large-scale data exfiltration; at least three production pipelines were impacted by transient credential errors. Paging thresholds triggered for SRE and Security on 2026-03-09 08:12 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 2026-03-09 07:58 UTC: User 'mike.leung@redwood.com' clicked a shared Google Drive link from unknown sender and accepted OAuth consent for 'QuickSync Backup' app.
~10 minutes later: Monitoring alert - spike in /v1/provision/serviceAccount POSTs from oauth-client-id 'quick-sync-xyz'.
Replays of API traffic show oauth2 token exchange followed by calls to /internal/infra/provision with X-Client-Id: quick-sync-xyz.
Attempts to replicate by consenting to the app from a test account produced the same token-exchange pattern (replay preserved in audit snapshots).
logs: audit.log entries: event_id=ev-20260309-0810, actor=oauth:quick-sync-xyz, action=serviceAccount.create, region=us-east-1, resource=sa-prod-sync-7a
auth.log: oauth.exchange success for user_id=U-48902, client_id=quick-sync-xyz, scope=openid,service_account:provision
network: outbound connections to 185.38.247.11:443 (Ukraine-hosted), repeated TLS sessions within 5m window
stacktrace from svc-provision: WARN - failed-rotate-temp-key for sa-prod-sync-7a (retryable, later rotation succeeded)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: user-consent to a malicious OAuth app permitted client-side provisioning via a scoped service account API (least-privilege gap in oauth-to-service mapping).
SAML/SSO logs show no direct IdP compromise; the user authenticated via normal SSO flow before consenting to the external app.
Service accounts created had short TTL and were used to trigger deploy pipelines for two low-priority non-customer-facing services; no sensitive blob storage reads observed in the first 90 minutes.

IP addresses correlate with known suspicious hosting provider; reverse DNS inconsistent with vendor claims. Endpoint team captured pcap of suspicious egress (stored in /sec/evidence/INT-903321/pcap_20260309.pcap).
Related tickets INT-70319 (oauth refresh spikes) and INT-121234 (possible session cookie capture) were linked for further context; pattern overlaps with previous external-consent incidents.
mitigation_actions: Disabled OAuth client_id 'quick-sync-xyz' in the org admin console at 2026-03-09 08:35 UTC.
Rotated service-account keys for impacted accounts and revoked any active tokens issued to those accounts.
Applied temporary org policy to block third-party OAuth app consent for anyone without SRE/Security approval.
Isolated the two provisioned service accounts and rolled back the two deploys they initiated; deploy pipeline owners notified.
Initiated targeted passwordless MFA check and re-evaluation of SSO session tokens for user 'mike.leung@redwood.com'.
follow_up_tasks: Ticket: Create policy update RFC to restrict oauth-to-service provisioning mappings (owner: IAM team).
Audit: Expand alerting for service-account.create originating from external oauth clients (owner: Monitoring).
Compliance: Log and export all audit records to secure bucket for potential post-incident review (owner: Security Ops).
User training: Notify affected user and run brief phishing awareness and OAuth consent guidance session (owner: People Ops).

Security to lead policy change for OAuth consent mappings and Monitoring to add alerts for oauth-originated provisioning. User education scheduled. Longer-term IAM changes tracked as follow-up tasks; incident will be closed once RFC implemented.
